title: The Memory Palace
subtitle: Store items in rooms of your imagination and walk through to recall everything!

sections.prompt: Can you remember 5 items placed in random spots without writing them down?
sections.subtext: Ancient Greek orators used this exact spatial superpower 2,500 years ago!

panels.text: Mia has to give a speech with 5 key points. Every time she practices, her mind goes completely blank!
Professor Piko smiles: 'You have a giant supercomputer in your brain dedicated just to navigation! Let's build a Memory Palace in your bedroom.'
Pick 5 fixed stations in order: 1. Door 🚪 -> 2. Bed 🛏️ -> 3. Desk 🖥️ -> 4. Bookshelf 📚 -> 5. Window 🪟.
When I place a glowing Key at the Door, a bouncing Robot on my Bed, and a flying Rocket on my Desk, I just walk through my room to remember!
BOOP! Step inside your palace simulation and test your spatial navigation recall!

sections.title: The Method of Loci (Palace Route)
sections.summary: 1. Pick a familiar room  |  2. Fix a clockwise path through 5 landmarks  |  3. Place vivid items at each spot  |  4. Walk the path to retrieve

interactions: Drag each object onto its specific room station
Walk through the loci in order to verify your mental journey
config.completionCondition: All 5 objects placed at their correct loci stations

questions.prompt: Why is it important to always walk through your Memory Palace in the exact same order?

options.label: So you can recall items in exact sequence without missing any station
Because the objects might disappear if you turn backwards
Because doors can only be opened from the outside

hints: A fixed route keeps your thoughts organized and guarantees 100% recall completeness.

questions.prompt: Arrange the Bedroom Palace stations in the correct clockwise order:
hints: Start from the door where you enter the room.

questions.prompt: In the simulation, which item was placed on the Bed 🛏️?
hints: Picture the robot jumping on the mattress!

questions.prompt: Which item was placed by the Sunny Window 🪟 catching the outdoor breeze?
hints: What flies in the sky right outside the window?
